title: Implement squash-chain landing in the gate (D69, option B)
summary: Implement option B from docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md (D69): add athena.candidate/2 with base_fingerprint and previous_job, have the core write them, and make the gate's landing, jobs and history checks accept a linear chain of jobs in one squash commit. Add the tests the design lists and update the docs from proposed to implemented.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests plus markdown docs.
Chain tests added; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The design and its two reviews already exist; the build follows them.
The vague request was resolved from the repository's design doc section 5.
The rule is enforced in the gate's landing check, not prose.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.

assumptions: 'The squash-chain landing' means implementing option B of docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md (D69), the follow-up work listed in its section 5.
The design's stated assumption on previous_job (core derives latest landed job in base history) is accepted as written.
Intermediate details such as the 'changes' field name are confirmed against the code by the producer.
Treated as one change even though large; the design's own ordering (test first) is followed.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena-data records.rs defines athena.candidate/2 with base_fingerprint and previous_job (optional), registered in AnyRecord and the schema-name table; /1 still parses; docs/records.md documents /2.

athena-core run.rs writes /2 candidates with base_fingerprint computed from the base commit and previous_job derived as the latest landed job in the base's history (absent if none); store.rs and every other AnyRecord::Candidate consumer handle /2.

invariant.rs landing replaces the single-job refusal with the chain check of design §4.2 (single job unchanged; multi-job needs one parent, /2 records, no .gitattributes change, one linear chain ordered by previous_job, head base equals parent fingerprint, last job equals landed tree, per-job checks for every job) using the §4.3 refusal messages.
jobs.rs check and the history walk accept and record every job of a chain, so repeating a chain job later is refused.

Tests are added first for a hand-built two-job chain, then for each refusal and case in design §5 item 4 (fork, unlinked job, broken link, /1 member, repeated fingerprints, rules-file change, two parents, partly landed chain, previous_job derivation, per-job check failures on a middle job).

docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md status, docs/design/athena-v0.md §7.3, docs/enforcement.md rows, docs/decisions.md D69 and CHANGELOG.md are updated to say the check is implemented. No governance file or records/ path changes.
Run cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo fmt --check from the repo root; all pass.

out_of_scope: Changes to athena.toml, workflows, .gitattributes or other governance files
Passing landing's refusal reason through the merge-commit path of check
Signing records to prevent forged chains
departures: Reference is for typical small jobs; this is a multi-crate schema and gate change with many tests, so cost, time and risk are higher.
